Clip 1.3:  BG Music: “Same mysterious tone…”  Narration: “Is kahani ka raasta…”
 - SFX: “Door creak”
THIS IS WRONG! Creates choppy, unprofessional audio!

---

### + CORRECT (BATCH audio approach):

  SCENE 1 - COMPLETE AUDIO PLAN

 BG MUSIC BLOCK:  CLIPS COVERED: 1.1 - 1.6 (ALL scene clips)  DURATION:
36 seconds total  TRACK: “Mystery Unfolding” by Trending Music  SOURCE:
https://pixabay.com/music/  NOTES: Fade in 1.1, continuous, fade out 1.6

NARRATION BLOCK:  CLIPS COVERED: 1.1 - 1.4 (First 4 clips only) 
DURATION: 24 seconds  ONE CONTINUOUS RECORDING: | “Faisalabad ke Aminpur
Bazaar mein ek haveli hai, | number 47. 35 saal pehle Professor Danish Mirza | yahan se
ghayab hue. Unke pote Zain ne dada ki | diary mein woh cipher dekh liya jo Kashmir ka
raasta dikhata hai.”  STYLE: Deep male, 50s, mysterious  Clips 1.5-1.6: SILENT (no
narration)
 SOUND EFFECTS (Per clip where needed):  Clip 1.1: “Birds chirping morning” -
Mixkit (0:00-0:06)  Clip 1.2: “Footsteps on stone” - Mixkit (0:02-0:05)  Clip 1.3:
None  Clip 1.4: “Old door creak” - Mixkit (0:03-0:05)  Clip 1.5: “Room ambience” -
Pixabay (throughout)  Clip 1.6: “Book pages turning” - Mixkit (0:02-0:04)

---

### AUDIO BATCH RULES:

  AUDIO TYPE | COVERAGE | FORMAT
  BG Music | 3-6 clips minimum | ONE track per block   | (entire
scene or | Exact track name +   | scene section) | source URL
  Narration | 3-5 clips | ONE continuous recording   | (not every
clip!) | Full text as single piece   | 60-70% clips = SILENT
  Sound Effects | Per clip | Only where needed   | (individual)
Exact name + source URL
  Dialogue | Per clip | Only where character   | (individual)
actually speaks

---

### MANDATORY: DRAMATIC NARRATION CHECK

    BEFORE finalizing ANY narration text, verify it’s   DRAMATIC, not
DRY!     DRY narration = Viewer gets bored = Clicks away!   DRAMATIC narration
= Viewer FEELS the story = Stays!  

### NARRATION STYLE CHECKLIST (USE FOR EVERY NARRATION):

SENSORY DETAILS? - “Raat thi” + “Raat ke 2 baje. Barf gir rahi thi. Haath kaanp rahe
the.”
EMOTION CONVEYED? - “Woh dar gaya” + “Uska dil itni tez dhadak raha tha ke
saans lena mushkil tha”

STAKES CLEAR? - “Mushkil tha” + “Agar 3 minute mein nahi bachaya, poora Kashmir
gulaam ban jayega”

TIME PRESSURE? - “Jaldi karna tha” + “Sirf 3 minute the. 3 minute. Aur 200 sipahi
100 kadam door.”

SHORT PUNCHY SENTENCES FOR TENSION? - Long flowing paragraph + “Woh ruka.
Saans roki. Andhera. Khamoshi. Phir… qadam ki awaaz.”

SPECIFIC NUMBERS? - “Bohat log”, “kuch waqt”, “door tak” + “23 log”, “3 minute”,
“200 kadam”
If ANY checkbox is empty → REWRITE the narration!

### VOICE DIRECTION (Include with narration):

For ElevenLabs/voice generation, ALWAYS specify:
TENSE MOMENTS: “Voice: Lower pitch, slower pace. Pause after key words. Example
delivery: ‘Sirf… [pause] 3 minute the.’”
EMOTIONAL MOMENTS: “Voice: Warmer, intimate. Let emotion break through. Example:
‘Dada ki aakhri yaad… [voice slightly cracks] woh mushkurahat.’”
REVELATION MOMENTS: “Voice: Building energy, then pause before reveal. Example: ‘Aur
jab usne khola… [long pause] sab badal gaya.’”
ACTION MOMENTS: “Voice: Faster, urgent, breathless. Example: ‘Bhaago! Ab! ABHI!’”

---

### SCENE-LEVEL AUDIO PLANNING:

**BEFORE generating clip prompts, plan audio for ENTIRE scene:**

SCENE X AUDIO PLAN:  Total clips: [X]  Total duration: [X] seconds |   BG
MUSIC: |  Clips covered: [X.1 - X.X] |  Track name: “[Exact name]” |  Source:
[URL] |   NARRATION: |  Clips covered: [X.1 - X.X] (or NONE) |  Silent
clips: [X.X - X.X] |  Full text: “[Complete narration]” |   SFX NEEDED: | 
Clip X.1: [Effect] or None |  Clip X.2: [Effect] or None |  … |   DIALOGUE:
 - Clip X.X: [Character]: “[Line]”  Other clips: None

---
### WHY BATCH APPROACH:

PROFESSIONAL AUDIO WORKFLOW:  BG Music: Downloaded once, laid across
timeline  Narration: Recorded once, placed across clips  SFX: Added individually
where needed  Result: Seamless, professional audio
PER-CLIP APPROACH (WRONG):  BG Music: Different description each clip =
inconsistent  Narration: Choppy sentences = unnatural  SFX: Same thing repeated
= redundant  Result: Amateur, choppy audio

---

### AUDIO vs VIDEO - CLEAR DISTINCTION:

VIDEO PROMPT handles:  Character VISUALLY speaking (lip sync)  Character
expressions WHILE speaking  Character body language during dialogue  Visual
reactions to sounds  Timing of actions with narration  ALL visual representation
of audio moments
AUDIO SECTION handles:  Actual voice generation prompts (for ElevenLabs, etc.) 
Background music generation prompts (for Suno AI, etc.)  Sound effect descriptions
(for Freesound, etc.)  Complete audio production guide

**BOTH sections must be complete for EVERY clip!**

---

### CRITICAL: Audio Pacing Rules (VERY IMPORTANT!)

**PROBLEM - Every clip having narration/dialogue:**

WRONG: Clip 1.1: Narration “Faisalabad ke is purane mohalle mein…” Clip 1.2:
Narration “…ek haveli thi jise log…” Clip 1.3: Narration “…Danish sahab rehte the…” Clip
1.4: Narration “…unka junoon tha kitabein…” Clip 1.5: Dialogue “Beta, pehle taleem
mukammal karo” Clip 1.6: Narration “Zain ne sun li…”
THIS IS EXHAUSTING! No breathing room. Feels artificial and non-engaging.


**+ CORRECT - Natural pacing with visual breathing room:**

Clip 1.1: PURE VISUAL  (opening hook, atmosphere, NO narration)
Clip 1.2: PURE VISUAL  (building mood, NO narration) Clip 1.3:
NARRATION STARTS  “Faisalabad ke is purane mohalle mein ek haveli thi…”
(begins) Clip 1.4: NARRATION CONTINUES  “…jise log ‘Kitaabon wala ghar’ kehte
the. Danish sahab…” (flows) Clip 1.5: NARRATION ENDS  “…yeh unka
junoon tha.” (completes) Clip 1.6: PURE VISUAL  (let the words sink
in, NO narration) Clip 1.7: PURE VISUAL  (emotional beat, visual
storytelling) Clip 1.8: NEW NARRATION STARTS  (fresh audio element begins)

---

### AUDIO PACING GUIDELINES:

| Clip Type | When to Use | Purpose |
|-----------|-------------|---------|
| **Pure Visual** | Opening shots, transitions, emotional beats, reactions |
Let visuals breathe, build atmosphere, process information |
| **Narration START** | Beginning a thought/story section | Introduce
information |
| **Narration CONTINUE** | Long narration spanning clips | Natural speech
flow |
| **Narration END** | Completing a thought | Allow processing time after |
| **Dialogue** | Character interaction | Story progression |
| **Reaction Shot** | After important dialogue | Show impact without words |
| **Silent Tension** | Before climax, dramatic moments | Build suspense |

---

### NARRATION DURATION RULES:

**How much narration fits in 6 seconds?**
- Slow, dramatic pace: 15-20 words
- Normal pace: 20-25 words
- Fast pace: 25-30 words (NOT recommended for cinematic feel)

**If narration is longer than 20-25 words:**
- SPLIT across multiple clips
- Mark clearly: "NARRATION STARTS", "NARRATION CONTINUES", "NARRATION ENDS"
- Visuals in each clip should match that portion of narration

**Example - Long Narration Split:**

Full narration (45 words - needs 2-3 clips): “Faisalabad ke is purane mohalle mein ek
haveli thi, jise log ‘Kitaabon wala ghar’ kehte the. Is haveli mein rehte the Danish sahab - ek
aisa insaan jisne apni poori zindagi ilm ki talaash mein guzaari.”
Clip 1.3 - NARRATION STARTS (16 words): “Faisalabad ke is purane mohalle mein ek haveli
thi, jise log ‘Kitaabon wala ghar’ kehte the.” Visual: Exterior of haveli, slow reveal
Clip 1.4 - NARRATION ENDS (18 words): “Is haveli mein rehte the Danish sahab - ek aisa
insaan jisne apni poori zindagi ilm ki talaash mein guzaari.” Visual: Interior, books, Danish
sahab’s study
---

### IDEAL AUDIO DISTRIBUTION (10-clip scene example):

Scene 1 (10 clips) - Opening:  Clip 1.1: PURE VISUAL  (atmosphere,
hook)  Clip 1.2: PURE VISUAL  (building mood)  Clip 1.3:
NARRATION STARTS  (intro begins)  Clip 1.4: NARRATION CONTINUES 
(story flows)  Clip 1.5: NARRATION ENDS  (thought completes)  Clip
1.6: PURE VISUAL  (breathing room)  Clip 1.7: NARRATION STARTS
 (new information)  Clip 1.8: NARRATION ENDS  (completes)
 - Clip 1.9: PURE VISUAL  (emotional beat)  Clip 1.10: PURE
VISUAL  (scene transition prep)
Result: 4 clips with narration, 6 clips pure visual This feels NATURAL and CINEMATIC!

---

### DIALOGUE PACING RULES:

**Don't cram dialogue into every clip!**

WRONG (machine-gun dialogue): Clip 5.1: Zain: “Yeh kya hai?” Clip 5.2: Hassan: “Pata
nahi, dikha” Clip 5.3: Zain: “Yeh to Dada ki cheez hai” Clip 5.4: Hassan: “Kya likha hai
ismein?”

CORRECT (natural pacing with reactions): Clip 5.1: Zain: “Yeh kya hai?” (surprised
discovery) Clip 5.2: PURE VISUAL - Hassan moving closer, examining (REACTION, no
dialogue) Clip 5.3: Hassan: “Pata nahi… dikha zara” (natural pause before response) Clip
5.4: PURE VISUAL - Both examining together (visual storytelling) Clip 5.5: Zain: “Yeh to…
Dada ki cheez lagti hai” (realization dawning)

---

### KEY AUDIO PACING PRINCIPLES:

1. **Not every clip needs words** - Silent moments are powerful
2. **Reactions don't need dialogue** - Show, don't tell
3. **Long narrations MUST be split** - Natural speech across clips
4. **After important information → breathing room** - Let it sink in
5. **Before dramatic moment → silence** - Build tension
6. **Dialogue needs realistic pauses** - People don't respond instantly
7. **Pure visual clips = 40-60% of scene** - Essential for cinematic feel
8. **Mark narration status** - START/CONTINUE/END for clarity

---
### FOR AUDIO SECTION IN PURE VISUAL CLIPS:

Even when there's NO narration/dialogue, Audio Section must include:

AUDIO (For External Audio Generation):
Type Content
BG Music [Continuing/New] - [Mood description]
Sound Effects [Environmental sounds: wind, birds, footsteps, etc.]
Narration None - Pure visual clip
Dialogue None - Pure visual clip
Ambient [Atmospheric sounds that enhance the mood]

grok_limitations.reference_logic:
## Reference Logic:
| Situation | What to Attach |
|-----------|----------------|
| Environment only (no character) | New image OR last frame |
| Hand/body visible (no face) | Last frame + describe clothing/skin in TEXT |
| Character FACE visible (first time in scene) | Generate NEW combined image
with character |
| Character FACE visible (continuing) | Last frame only |
| NEW character FACE appearing | Generate NEW combined image with new
character |
| **NEW important object/element appearing** | Generate NEW IMAGE including
that element |

---

### CHARACTER INTRODUCTION RULES (EXTREMELY IMPORTANT!)

**THE PROBLEM:**
AI writes "Zain enters the room" but FORGETS that:
1. Zain wasn't in previous frame
2. The DOOR wasn't even visible (was close-up on books!)
3. Camera position makes character entry IMPOSSIBLE

**REAL FAILURE EXAMPLE:**

Clip 1.6 ENDS: “Close-up on bookshelf section, books fill ENTIRE frame” (No door visible,
no empty space, just books!)
Clip 1.7: “Camera pulls back, Zain steps into room from doorway”

THIS IS IMPOSSIBLE!
 • Where is the door? It wasn’t in frame!
 • Where did Zain come from? He wasn’t visible!
 • How can camera “pull back” to reveal a door that wasn’t there?
 • Result: Zain APPEARS from nowhere - magic!

---

### CORRECT CHARACTER INTRODUCTION:

**When a CHARACTER enters a scene, you MUST do ONE of these:**

**OPTION A: Set Up the Entry Point in Previous Clip**

If Zain will enter through doorway in Clip 1.7:
Clip 1.6 must END with doorway VISIBLE: “…bookshelf fills center of frame. In the
BACKGROUND, visible through the gap between shelves, the main DOORWAY is partially
visible - empty, waiting, dusty light from the hallway beyond.”
Now Clip 1.7: “The empty doorway visible in background - a figure appears in it. Zain steps
through…”
Entry point was ESTABLISHED before character appears!


**OPTION B: Generate NEW IMAGE for Character Entry (RECOMMENDED)**

Clip 1.7 - CHARACTER FIRST APPEARANCE:
Reference: Generate NEW IMAGE - Character entering scene
IMAGE PROMPT (Gemini (Nano-Banana-Pro)): “Interior of the Pakistani haveli study room
from Clip 1.6. The same dark bookshelves, same golden lighting. But now the camera is
positioned showing the main doorway. Standing IN the doorway is Zain (28-year-old
Pakistani man, medium brown skin, short black hair, wearing olive green shirt) - he is mid-
step entering the room, his expression showing awe and melancholy as he sees the space
for the first time. The grand room stretches before him. 16:9 aspect ratio, photorealistic,
cinematic warm golden lighting.”

 Save as: Clip_1.7_image.png
Now VIDEO PROMPT uses this new image where Zain is ALREADY in frame!

**OPTION C: Add Transition Clip(s)**

Clip 1.6: Close-up on books Clip 1.6B: Camera pulls back, revealing more of room, doorway
comes into view (EMPTY) Clip 1.6C: Continuing pull back, doorway now prominent in
frame (still empty) Clip 1.7: A shadow appears in doorway, then Zain steps in

Gradual reveal of entry point, then character!


---

### CHARACTER INTRODUCTION CHECKLIST:

Before writing ANY clip where a character ENTERS or APPEARS:

Is the ENTRY POINT (door, hallway, window) visible in previous clip’s last frame?
 • If NO → You cannot have character enter from there!

Is there EMPTY SPACE in the previous frame where character will appear?
 • If NO → Character cannot appear there!

Was the previous clip a CLOSE-UP with no background visible?
 • If YES → You MUST either: a) Add transition clips to pull back and reveal entry point
 b) Generate NEW IMAGE with character already in scene

Have you generated a CHARACTER REFERENCE image?
 • If character’s FACE will be visible → Need reference OR new combined image

---

### EXAMPLES OF CHARACTER ENTRY:

**WRONG - Character appears from nowhere:**

Clip 5 ends: Close-up on desk items (fills frame) Clip 6: “Zain walks to the desk and picks up
the magnifying glass”

Where did Zain come from?! He wasn’t in frame!


**CORRECT - Character entry prepared:**

Clip 5 ends: “Close-up on desk items. In the blurred background, the doorway and part of
the room is visible.” Clip 6: Generate NEW IMAGE - Zain standing at desk OR Clip 5B:
Camera pulls back, Zain visible approaching desk Clip 6: Zain reaches the desk (continuous
from 5B)

Character entry is smooth and logical!


---

### SPATIAL LOGIC FOR CHARACTER ENTRY:

**Where CAN a character enter from?**
- Doorway (if visible in previous frame)
- Side of frame (if there's empty space on that side)
- Background (if background is visible, not close-up)

**Where can a character NOT enter from?**
- Nowhere - they cannot appear magically
- From behind camera (unless it's a POV shot)
- From areas not visible in previous frame
- From areas filled by objects (bookshelves, walls)

---

### THE GOLDEN RULE FOR CHARACTER INTRODUCTION:

**If the entry point is not visible → The character cannot enter!**

Either:
1. Make entry point visible in previous clip
2. Generate NEW IMAGE with character
3. Add transition clips
**NEVER write a character entering from an invisible location!**

---

### CRITICAL: New Element Introduction Rules

**THE PROBLEM:**
When you use last frame as reference but the next clip introduces something
NEW (object, area, detail) that WASN'T in the last frame, Video AI will:
- Generate the new thing randomly
- Make it "appear out of nowhere"
- Create jarring, unnatural transitions
- Break visual continuity

**REAL EXAMPLE OF THE PROBLEM:**

Clip 1.3: Wide shot of study room (bookshelves, desk, windows) Last frame: General room
view, NO locked cage visible
Clip 1.4: “Extreme close-up on locked brass cage with special books” Using:
Clip_1.3_lastframe.png as reference
RESULT: The locked cage appears OUT OF NOWHERE - like materializing from the wall!
Because it wasn’t in the reference image at all.

---

### SOLUTION: Three Approaches for New Elements

**APPROACH 1: Plant the Element in Previous Clip (BEST)**

If next clip will focus on something, make it VISIBLE in current clip:

Clip 1.3 VIDEO PROMPT must include: “…bookshelves reaching ceiling, and in the far left
corner, barely visible in shadow, an ornate brass cage built into the shelving protecting
several ancient books…”
Clip 1.3 LAST FRAME DESCRIPTION must include: “…the locked brass cage section visible
in the left portion of frame, partially in shadow, hinting at protected knowledge…”
NOW Clip 1.4 can zoom into something that ALREADY EXISTS in frame!

**APPROACH 2: Generate NEW IMAGE for New Element**

When introducing major new visual element, create fresh image:

Clip 1.4 - NEW element (locked cage) featured:
Reference: Generate NEW IMAGE - New important element being introduced
IMAGE PROMPT (Gemini (Nano-Banana-Pro)): “Close-up view inside the Pakistani haveli
study. Focus on an ornate brass cage built directly into dark mahogany bookshelves. The
cage has intricate Islamic patterns, tarnished green with age, a heavy antique lock covered
in undisturbed dust. Behind the brass bars, five ancient leather-bound books with gold
Arabic script on spines. Surrounding regular bookshelves visible in background for context.
Golden light catching dust particles near the cage. 16:9 aspect ratio, photorealistic,
cinematic warm golden lighting.”

 Save as: Clip_1.4_image.png
Then VIDEO PROMPT uses this NEW image as reference.

**APPROACH 3: Add Transition Clip (For Major Reveals)**

When element reveal is dramatic, add a transition:

Clip 1.3: Wide room shot → Ends with: “camera settling, hint of something metallic glinting
in far left bookshelf”
Clip 1.3B (TRANSITION): Camera slowly panning left → “Camera drifts toward the left
bookshelf section, gradually revealing an ornate brass structure…” → Ends with: “Locked
brass cage now prominent in right side of frame”
Clip 1.4: Close-up on cage (NOW it’s established and natural!)

---

### WHEN TO USE EACH APPROACH:

| Situation | Best Approach |
|-----------|---------------|
| Small detail being featured next | Approach 1: Plant in previous clip |
| Major new object/area | Approach 2: Generate new image |
| Dramatic reveal moment | Approach 3: Add transition clip |
| Continuing same elements | Just use last frame |

---

### NEW ELEMENT CHECKLIST (Before Writing Each Clip):

Before writing any clip prompt, ask:

Does this clip introduce ANY new visual element?
Was this element visible in the previous clip's last frame?
If NO → Choose an approach:
 - Plant it in previous clip's last frame description
 - Generate NEW IMAGE for this clip
 - Add a transition clip
NEVER assume Video AI will correctly generate something not in reference!

---

### EXAMPLES OF ELEMENTS THAT NEED SPECIAL HANDLING:

**Objects:**
- Locked cage/cabinet (if not in previous frame)
- Hidden drawer being opened
- Book/map being discovered
- Any prop that will be focused on

**Areas:**
- Different section of room
- Hidden corner or alcove
- Behind furniture
- Through a doorway

**Details:**
- Inscriptions on objects
- Specific book titles
- Dust patterns
- Any close-up detail

---

### PRACTICAL EXAMPLE - CORRECT WAY:

**Original Problem Clips (WRONG):**

Clip 1.3: Wide room shot Last frame: General room, no cage Clip 1.4: Close-up on locked
cage Result: Cage appears from nowhere -


**Fixed Version (CORRECT):**

**Anchor Image Method - Plant in Previous:**

Clip 1.3 VIDEO PROMPT (updated): “…The camera slowly pans across the magnificent
room, passing the towering bookshelves. In the far left section of the shelving, partially
shadowed, an unusual brass cage structure is barely visible - clearly protecting something
important within…”
Clip 1.3 LAST FRAME: “Wide view with brass cage visible in left portion of frame, partially
in shadow, creating curiosity”
Clip 1.4 VIDEO PROMPT: “Starting from the wide view (from attached image where cage is
visible on left), camera slowly dollies in toward the brass cage…” Result: Smooth, natural
transition +


**Anchor Image Method - New Image:**

Clip 1.4: Reference: Generate NEW IMAGE - New element being introduced
IMAGE PROMPT: “Close-up of ornate brass cage in mahogany bookshelf, ancient books
inside, tarnished lock, dust particles in golden light, rest of study room visible in soft
background…”
VIDEO PROMPT: Uses new image, cage is established from start Result: Clean introduction
of new element +


---

### STRICT RULE:

**If the next clip features ANYTHING that wasn't clearly visible in the
current clip's last frame → You MUST either:**
1. Update current clip to include that element in last frame
2. Generate a NEW IMAGE for the next clip
3. Add a transition clip

**NEVER hope that Video AI will magically create continuity!**

acting_system.7layer_acting_system_is_designed:
7-layer acting system is designed for PLANNING — but sending
all 7 layers simultaneously to Video AI OVERLOADS it.

FOR VIDEO PROMPTS, USE THIS 3-TIER SYSTEM:
acting_system.tier_1_primary_action_detailed:
TIER 1: PRIMARY ACTION (detailed, 2-3 sentences)
 What is the MAIN thing this character DOES in this clip?
 Describe it with clear start → middle → end.
acting_system.tier_2_emotional_state_1:
TIER 2: EMOTIONAL STATE (1 sentence)
 What is the character FEELING? One clear emotion.
 NOT: "eyes narrow, brows furrow, jaw tenses, shoulders rise"
 BUT: "His expression shifts from alert caution to sudden alarm"
 Let the AI interpret how to show that emotion!
acting_system.tier_3_physics_3_specific:
TIER 3: PHYSICS (3 specific elements)
 Pick 3 from: breathing, weight shift, fabric, hair,
 muscle tension, blinking, balance
 Write one line per physics element.

THAT'S IT! 3 tiers maximum.
AI handles the micro-details BETTER when given clear emotion
versus 7 simultaneous body-part instructions.

EXAMPLE — OLD (overloaded 7-layer):
"Eyes: focused upper-left for 2 sec then shift to sandook for
2 sec then lift forward for 2 sec; Eyebrows: slight furrow
tightening at mid-clip; Mouth: closed jaw set; Head: mostly
still 10-degree turn; Shoulders: squared slight rise at mid-
clip; Posture: firm balanced 5-degree lean; Hands: RIGHT lowers
hovers LEFT near sash. Micro-expression: jaw twitch at 3 sec."

EXAMPLE — NEW (focused 3-tier):
"PRIMARY ACTION: His right hand slowly lowers toward the sandook
lid, fingers spreading as they approach. Hand stops just above
the surface, hovering with visible tension.

EMOTION: Controlled determination masking deep unease — the face
of a young leader forcing himself to stay calm under pressure.

PHYSICS: Chest rises with a slow, deep breath held at the top.
Weight settles firmly onto front foot. The maroon sash shifts
slightly with his movement."

The NEW version will produce BETTER results because:
- AI focuses on ONE clear action (hand lowering)
- AI interprets emotion naturally (doesn't fight 7 instructions)
- Physics make the character feel alive
- Total is ~80 words, not 150 of conflicting micro-instructions

acting_system.clip_type_specific_tips:
CLIP TYPE SPECIFIC TIPS

ESTABLISHING / WIDE (no faces):
- Focus on ENVIRONMENT motion: torch flames, dust, wind
- Camera movement can be bolder (drone drift, crane)
- Human figures move as SILHOUETTES — "small figures walk
 with visible leg movement, torches sway in wind"
- Add atmosphere: "dust particles drift in torchlight"

MEDIUM SHOTS (1 person):
- Use full 3-tier acting system
- Camera: push in OR static with handheld drift
- Always include 3 physics elements
- Face lock essential

CLOSE-UPS (face emotion):
- PRIMARY ACTION = emotional shift, NOT physical movement
- "His expression transitions from guarded calm to barely
 contained fear" > describing individual facial muscles
- Add: "natural blink" and "subtle jaw tension"
- Camera: STATIC or very gentle push in
- Face lock CRITICAL — "face stays pin-sharp throughout"

DETAIL / INSERT (objects):
- Focus on OBJECT physics: dust settling, metal glinting,
 wood creaking, fabric rippling
- No faces needed = no face problems
- Camera: static macro or very slow push in
- Best results: describe particle physics around object

ACTION / CHAOS (multiple elements):
- Pick THE most important action as primary
- Other actions are "secondary: [brief hint]"
- "Arrows streak across frame while [primary action]"
- Keep camera movement simple (static or slow push)
- More motion in scene = less camera movement needed
acting_system.common_video_ai_problems_and:
COMMON VIDEO AI PROBLEMS AND FIXES

PROBLEM: Characters SLIDE instead of walk
FIX: "visible leg movement, feet lift off ground, natural gait"

PROBLEM: Faces BLUR or MORPH
FIX: Add Face Lock paragraph + keep clips to 6 sec max
 + prefer close-ups with 1 character only

PROBLEM: Objects APPEAR or DISAPPEAR
FIX: Add full Stability Locks section

PROBLEM: Colors SHIFT during clip
FIX: "Colors and lighting remain exactly as in attached image,
 zero color drift, zero exposure change"

PROBLEM: Movement looks MECHANICAL / robotic
FIX: Add 3+ physics elements (breathing, weight, fabric)
 + use emotion words not body-part instructions

PROBLEM: Too much CHAOS / uncontrolled motion
FIX: Reduce to 1 hero action. Add "everything else holds still"
 Use "gently" "subtly" "slightly" for secondary motion

PROBLEM: NOTHING happens (too static)
FIX: Use intensity adverbs: "noticeably", "clearly", "with force"
 Make sure primary action has clear start → end states

PROBLEM: LIP SYNC looks wrong
FIX: Use phonetic breakdown with syllable shapes and duration

PROBLEM: Clip DOESN'T MATCH next clip (continuity break)
FIX: Strong ENDS WITH section describing exact final state
 Export last frame as reference for next clip

PROBLEM: AI generates CUT or FADE (not continuous)
FIX: "Single continuous shot from start to end. No cuts, no
 fades, no dissolves, no transitions. One unbroken take."
acting_system.grokspecific_prompt_optimization:
GROK-SPECIFIC PROMPT OPTIMIZATION:
Grok Imagine uses the Aurora engine for Image-to-Video.
It works DIFFERENTLY from other video AIs.
Follow these Grok-specific rules for BEST results!

⚠️ THE DUAL MODE TEMPLATES (Template A: Subtle 80-100 words,
Template B: Action 10-25 words) are defined above in the 
"BEFORE WRITING ANY VIDEO PROMPT" section. USE THOSE TEMPLATES.
The rules below are ADDITIONAL Grok-specific optimizations.


 SCENE TYPE DETECTION (MANDATORY FIRST STEP!):
BEFORE writing ANY Grok video prompt, FIRST identify
the SCENE TYPE. This determines EVERYTHING:
prompt length, detail level, what YOU control vs
what GROK controls.
TWO MODES — each has opposite rules!
acting_system.mode_1_subtle_dialogue_emotional:
MODE 1: SUBTLE / DIALOGUE / EMOTIONAL SCENES

Keywords: conversation, whisper, reaction, thinking,
observing, emotional moment, revelation, quiet tension
YOU CONTROL: expression, camera, body language, audio,
dialogue volume, environment details
GROK FOLLOWS: your detailed instructions
PROMPT LENGTH: 80-100 words
DETAIL LEVEL: HIGH — describe expression, camera,
body language, audio, timing
acting_system.mode_2_action_combat_physical:
MODE 2: ACTION / COMBAT / PHYSICAL IMPACT SCENES

Keywords: fight, hit, swing, charge, attack, clash,
chase, jump, throw, crash, battle, combat
YOU CONTROL: WHO does WHAT to WHOM and HOW HARD
GROK CONTROLS: impact physics, debris, camera angle,
character reactions, environment response, sound
PROMPT LENGTH: 10-25 words
DETAIL LEVEL: MINIMAL — action verb + target + degree
word ONLY. NO impact results, NO camera, NO reactions.

WHY TWO MODES?
Grok handles subtle scenes and action scenes with 
OPPOSITE approaches:

SUBTLE: Grok NEEDS detailed direction. Without it, 
expressions become random, dialogue becomes screaming/
whispering randomly, camera does unpredictable things.
→ MORE detail = BETTER result.

ACTION: Grok ALREADY knows how to choreograph combat.
When you over-describe action, Grok gets CONFUSED — 
characters morph, extra people spawn, physics break.
→ LESS detail = BETTER result.

TESTED PROOF:
- 105-word combat prompt = morphing, spawning, unrealistic
- 15-word combat prompt = perfect shield impact, debris, 
 realistic reactions — Grok decided everything itself
- 100-word dialogue prompt = controlled expression, proper 
 whisper volume, stable background

acting_system.grokspecific_rules_for_subtle_scenes:
GROK-SPECIFIC RULES FOR SUBTLE SCENES:
1. MAX 100 WORDS — Grok loses focus beyond this!
2. FIRST 30 WORDS = Camera + main action (highest priority)
3. NEGATIVE PROMPTS DON'T WORK — Grok ignores "no fog" etc.
 Only describe what you WANT (positive instructions only)
4. DEGREE WORDS are powerful — slowly, rapidly, gently, 
 forcefully, subtly, violently, dramatically, powerfully
5. ALWAYS SPECIFY AUDIO — or Grok adds GENERIC music!
 "Audio: wind, torch crackle, no music" prevents this
6. Use "Unfixed lens" in Grok settings for camera movement
7. Grok supports: push-in, pull-out, pan, tilt, orbit, 
 follow/track, handheld, static, crane up/down, dolly

SUBTLE SCENE TEMPLATE:
TEMPLATE 
[Camera movement + endpoint]. [Subject identified by 
visual features performs key action with degree word]. 
[Face description: ONE emotion word — mouth state, jaw 
state]. [ONE body language action]. [1-2 environment 
physics]. Background stays sharp and in focus with full 
detail throughout. Single continuous shot.
Audio: [specific sounds], [dialogue with volume word 
if any], no music.
ENDS WITH: [final state description].
END TEMPLATE 

SUBTLE SCENE EXAMPLE (Messenger — TESTED +):
"High angle looking down at the kneeling messenger. 
Slow push-in ending at his chest level. His hands 
tremble visibly as he raises the empty open box 
slightly higher. Mouth stays closed, jaw clenched 
tight, brow furrowed — suppressed fear only. Chest 
rises and falls with slow controlled breathing. At 
second three his lips barely part as he murmurs in 
a low shaky whisper: 'Shahi Mohar... chori ho gayi, 
Jahanpanah.' Head stays bowed throughout. Torch glow 
sways gently on the walls. Fine dust drifts through 
the single light beam. Background stays sharp and in 
focus with full detail. Single continuous shot.
Audio: barely audible whisper with soft hall echo, 
faint cloth rustling, no music.
ENDS WITH: messenger still, box raised, silence."

mode_2_action_combat_scene.mode_2_action_combat:
MODE 2: ACTION / COMBAT SCENE SYSTEM (10-25 words)
 FOR ACTION SCENES: LESS IS MORE!
Grok ALREADY knows how to choreograph combat.
The more you describe, the WORSE the result.
15 words beat 105 words in EVERY test.
YOU define the ACTION.
GROK handles the IMPACT.
mode_2_action_combat_scene.action_scene_formula_tested:
ACTION SCENE FORMULA (TESTED & CONFIRMED!):

[Subject] + [Action Verb] + [Target] + [Degree Word]
mode_2_action_combat_scene.thats_it_nothing_else: That's it. Nothing else. 10-25 words MAXIMUM.
mode_2_action_combat_scene.you_define_4_things:
YOU DEFINE (4 things only):
WHO — subject (the warrior, the soldier, the rider)
DOES WHAT — action verb (swings, thrusts, slams, kicks)
TO WHOM/WHAT — target (shield, enemy, gate, wall)
HOW HARD — degree word (very hard, with full force, 
 violently, with massive strength)
mode_2_action_combat_scene.grok_decides_everything_else:
GROK DECIDES (everything else):
Impact physics (how shield breaks, how debris flies)
Camera angle and movement (best angle for action)
Character reactions (how target reacts to hit)
Environment response (dust, sparks, rain spray)
Sound design (impact sounds, cries, environmental)
Debris and particle effects
Body mechanics and follow-through
mode_2_action_combat_scene.never_add_to_action:
NEVER ADD TO ACTION PROMPTS:
Impact results — "shield shatters into pieces"
 → Grok over-interprets, creates bomb explosion
Camera instructions — "camera orbits rapidly"
 → Grok gets confused, picks wrong angle
Victim reactions — "soldier falls backward screaming"
 → Grok SPAWNS new characters
Debris descriptions — "sparks fly everywhere"
 → Grok creates unrealistic particle effects
Environment reactions — "ground shakes from impact"
 → Grok morphs the environment
Other characters — "surrounding soldiers flinch"
 → Grok ADDS extra soldiers that weren't in image
Sound descriptions — let Grok auto-generate
Background instructions — Grok preserves naturally
mode_2_action_combat_scene.why_this_works:
WHY THIS WORKS:
Grok's Aurora engine has built-in physics simulation.
When you say "hits shield very hard" — Grok ALREADY 
KNOWS what happens: debris, impact, reaction. But when 
you DESCRIBE what should happen, Grok tries to follow 
YOUR physics instead of ITS physics = unrealistic result.
mode_2_action_combat_scene.think_of_it_like:
Think of it like telling a stunt coordinator:
"Hit the shield hard" → coordinator creates epic stunt
"Hit the shield, then shield breaks at 45 degrees, 
 three pieces fly left, dust rises 2 feet, enemy 
 stumbles back 3 steps" → awkward forced stunt
mode_2_action_combat_scene.example_1_mace_vs:
Example 1 — Mace vs Shield:
"The warrior swings his mace very hard onto the 
nearest soldier's shield."
(13 words — PERFECT combat result with impact, debris,
 reactions all generated naturally by Grok)
mode_2_action_combat_scene.example_2_sword_strike:
Example 2 — Sword Strike:
"The knight slashes his sword across the enemy's 
chest armor with full force."
(14 words)
mode_2_action_combat_scene.example_3_spear_thrust:
Example 3 — Spear Thrust:
"The soldier drives his spear into the wooden 
barricade with massive strength."
(13 words)
mode_2_action_combat_scene.example_4_shield_bash:
Example 4 — Shield Bash:
"The guard rams his shield into the attacker's 
body very forcefully."
(12 words)
mode_2_action_combat_scene.example_5_arrow_impact:
Example 5 — Arrow Impact:
"The arrow strikes the stone pillar with great 
speed and force."
(12 words)
mode_2_action_combat_scene.degree_words_for_action:
DEGREE WORDS FOR ACTION (use these!):
very hard, with full force, with massive strength,
violently, forcefully, with brutal impact, with 
great power, with tremendous speed, fiercely,
with all his strength
mode_2_action_combat_scene.universal_grok_rules_apply: UNIVERSAL GROK RULES (Apply to BOTH Modes):
mode_2_action_combat_scene.imagetovideo_contradiction_rule_critical:
IMAGE-TO-VIDEO CONTRADICTION RULE (CRITICAL!):
Video prompt MUST NOT contradict the attached image!
Grok SEES the image. If your prompt says something
different from what's IN the image, Grok gets confused
and produces morphing, spawning, or artifacts.
mode_2_action_combat_scene.rules:
RULES:
1. If image has a MAN, prompt must NOT say "woman"
2. If image has a FOREST, prompt must NOT say "desert"
3. If image has 4 soldiers, prompt must NOT describe 10
4. If character faces LEFT, prompt must NOT say "faces right"
5. If character holds SWORD, prompt must NOT say "holds spear"
6. NEVER mention characters/objects NOT visible in the image
 → Grok will try to GENERATE them = spawn artifacts
7. NEVER describe the camera from an angle that contradicts 
 the image perspective (image is front view but prompt 
 says "camera follows from behind" = disaster)
mode_2_action_combat_scene.what_happens_when_you:
WHAT HAPPENS WHEN YOU CONTRADICT:
- Mention person not in image → Grok SPAWNS random figure
- Describe wrong weapon → Grok MORPHS existing weapon
- Wrong background → Grok tries to CHANGE environment
- Wrong camera angle → Grok warps perspective
mode_2_action_combat_scene.safe_approach_only_describe:
SAFE APPROACH: Only describe what CHANGES from the image.
Everything static in the image will stay automatically.
mode_2_action_combat_scene.expression_preservation_rule:
EXPRESSION PRESERVATION RULE:
When the image already has a SPECIFIC expression and
you want to KEEP it in the video, you MUST describe
the face DIRECTLY — never say "as in the image".
Grok ignores meta-instructions like "face stays as in
the image." It only follows DESCRIPTIONS.
mode_2_action_combat_scene.wrong_metainstruction_grok_ignores:
WRONG (meta-instruction, Grok ignores):
"Face stays exactly as in the image"
"Expression matches the reference"
"Keep the same look from the photo"
mode_2_action_combat_scene.right_direct_face_description:
RIGHT (direct face description):
"Mouth stays closed, jaw clenched tight, brow furrowed 
 — suppressed fear only"
"Eyes narrowed, lips pressed together — cold assessment"
"Mouth slightly open, eyebrows raised — frozen shock"
mode_2_action_combat_scene.rule_describe_the_actual:
RULE: Describe the ACTUAL face state you want. 
Grok follows descriptions, not references.
mode_2_action_combat_scene.expression_escalation_prevention:
EXPRESSION ESCALATION PREVENTION:
When image has a CALM/CONTROLLED expression but the 
scene involves intense emotion (fear, anger, grief):
mode_2_action_combat_scene.danger_grok_will_escalate:
DANGER: Grok will ESCALATE the expression to maximum!
 - Image shows quiet dread → Grok makes SCREAMING face
 - Image shows controlled anger → Grok makes RAGING face
 - Image shows sadness → Grok makes WAILING face
mode_2_action_combat_scene.fix_use_calm_emotion:
FIX: Use CALM emotion words even for intense scenes:
ESCALATING WORDS | + CONTROLLED WORDS
(Grok goes to max) | (Grok keeps it subtle)
terrified | quiet dread
desperate | contained urgency
agonized | still pain
furious | cold anger
devastated | deep stillness of grief
panicked | frozen tension
hysterical | held-back emotion
mode_2_action_combat_scene.when_to_use_escalating:
WHEN TO USE ESCALATING vs CONTROLLED:
- Action/combat scenes: escalating words OK (Grok should 
 go big — "fierce roar", "furious strike")
- Subtle/dialogue scenes: ALWAYS use controlled words 
 (Grok must stay subtle — "quiet dread", "still pain")
mode_2_action_combat_scene.expression_intensity_scale:
EXPRESSION INTENSITY SCALE:
AI ALWAYS defaults to Level 5 (maximum intensity)!
If you say "fear" + "speaking" → AI generates SCREAMING.
You MUST specify intensity level or AI goes maximum.
mode_2_action_combat_scene.level_1_microexpression_barely:
LEVEL 1 — MICRO-EXPRESSION (barely visible):
"A flicker of [emotion] crosses his face, almost 
 imperceptible. Face appears nearly neutral."
Use for: hidden feelings, poker face, professional mask
mode_2_action_combat_scene.level_2_suppressed_holding:
LEVEL 2 — SUPPRESSED (holding it in):
"[Emotion] visible in his eyes but mouth stays closed, 
 jaw tight. He is holding it in."
Use for: fear while trying to be brave, anger while 
staying professional, grief while maintaining composure
mode_2_action_combat_scene.level_3_visible_clearly:
LEVEL 3 — VISIBLE (clearly showing):
"[Emotion] clearly visible on his face. [One facial 
 feature change]."
Use for: natural reactions, moderate emotional moments
mode_2_action_combat_scene.level_4_strong_intense:
LEVEL 4 — STRONG (intense but controlled):
"Strong [emotion] on his face. [Two facial features 
 change]. Body language reinforces the feeling."
Use for: confrontations, major revelations, high stakes
mode_2_action_combat_scene.level_5_extreme_screaming:
LEVEL 5 — EXTREME (screaming, crying, raging):
"Full [emotion] — [open mouth/tears/clenched teeth]. 
 Entire body expresses the feeling."
Use for: battle cries, devastating loss, explosive rage
→ THIS IS AI DEFAULT! Only use when you actually WANT max!
mode_2_action_combat_scene.rule_always_identify_the:
RULE: Always identify the CORRECT level for your scene.
If you need Level 2 (suppressed fear for whisper scene)
but don't specify, AI will generate Level 5 (screaming).
mode_2_action_combat_scene.background_preservation_rule:
BACKGROUND PRESERVATION RULE:
Grok may BLUR or SOFTEN background by default to create 
"cinematic" depth of field. This looks bad in most scenes.
mode_2_action_combat_scene.for_subtle_scenes_always:
FOR SUBTLE SCENES — always add this line:
"Background stays sharp and in focus with full detail 
 throughout."
mode_2_action_combat_scene.for_action_scenes_do:
FOR ACTION SCENES — do NOT add this line.
Let Grok decide. Action scenes benefit from natural 
motion blur and Grok handles it well.
mode_2_action_combat_scene.what_causes_background_blur:
WHAT CAUSES BACKGROUND BLUR:
- Saying "background stays in place" → Grok reads as 
 "background not important" → blurs it
- Over-focusing on subject → Grok de-prioritizes background
- Not mentioning background at all → Grok decides randomly
mode_2_action_combat_scene.fix_sharp_and_in:
FIX: "sharp and in focus with full detail" explicitly 
tells Grok to render background at full quality.
mode_2_action_combat_scene.grok_objectcharacter_spawning_prevention:
GROK OBJECT/CHARACTER SPAWNING PREVENTION:
The #1 problem: characters and objects APPEAR or VANISH!
mode_2_action_combat_scene.causes:
CAUSES:
1. Mentioning characters NOT in image → Grok CREATES them
2. Describing reactions of background characters → Grok 
 SPAWNS new characters to "react" 
3. Asking for new objects → Grok generates them, sometimes
 replacing existing objects
mode_2_action_combat_scene.prevention_rules:
PREVENTION RULES:
1. Only mention characters/objects VISIBLE in the image
2. Do NOT describe reactions of secondary characters
3. Do NOT ask for objects that aren't in the image
4. For subtle scenes: "Background stays sharp and in focus 
 with full detail throughout" (prevents morphing)
5. For action scenes: say NOTHING about background 
 (Grok preserves automatically when prompt is short)
mode_2_action_combat_scene.what_to_do_about:
WHAT TO DO ABOUT SECONDARY CHARACTERS:
If image has 5 soldiers in background:
"The surrounding soldiers flinch and step back"
 → Grok ADDS more soldiers
Say nothing about them → Grok animates them naturally
Or for subtle scenes: "All other figures remain still"
mode_2_action_combat_scene.grok_hands_small_objects:
GROK HANDS & SMALL OBJECTS WARNING:
Hands interacting with small objects = Grok's WEAKEST 
area. Fingers morph, objects distort, physics break.
mode_2_action_combat_scene.safe_actions:
SAFE ACTIONS:
Hand rests on large surface (table, armrest, wall)
Hand grips large weapon (sword, mace, spear shaft)
Hand makes fist or opens flat
Hand gestures (pointing, waving, beckoning)
Arms cross, hands on hips, hands behind back
mode_2_action_combat_scene.risky_actions_avoid_if:
RISKY ACTIONS (avoid if possible):
Fingers manipulating small objects (coins, rings, beads)
Hand picking up something delicate
Two hands interacting with same small object
Close-up of fingers doing detailed work
mode_2_action_combat_scene.if_you_must_show:
IF YOU MUST SHOW HANDS WITH OBJECTS:
Keep hands still: "His hand rests motionless on [object]"
Don't animate the interaction. Let the hand be a 
static anchor while other things move.
mode_2_action_combat_scene.negativetopositive_conversion_mandatory:
NEGATIVE-TO-POSITIVE CONVERSION (MANDATORY!):
Grok IGNORES all negative instructions. EVERY negative 
statement MUST be rewritten as a positive statement before 
putting it in a Grok video prompt.
mode_2_action_combat_scene.conversion_table:
CONVERSION TABLE:
NEGATIVE (Grok ignores) | + POSITIVE (Grok follows)
"no morphing" | "All elements maintain exact
 appearance throughout"
"no new objects appear" | "Scene contains only existing
 elements from the image"
"no scene change" | "Single continuous scene
 maintained throughout"
"no fog" | "Air remains clean and clear"
"no color drift" | "Colors stay locked to image"
"second hand does not move" | "Clock hands remain completely
 frozen and still throughout"
"no cuts, no transitions" | "Single continuous unbroken take"
"no extra people" | "Only the existing figures remain
 visible throughout"
"don't move the object" | "Object stays fixed in its exact
 position throughout"
"no blur on face" | "Face remains sharp and in focus"
mode_2_action_combat_scene.exception_no_music_in:
EXCEPTION: "no music" in the Audio line IS the one negative 
that works in Grok, because it's an audio instruction, not a 
visual instruction. Keep using "Audio: [sounds], no music."
mode_2_action_combat_scene.before_finalizing_any_grok:
BEFORE FINALIZING ANY GROK VIDEO PROMPT:
Scan for ANY word: "no", "not", "don't", "never", "without"
→ If found in visual instructions → REWRITE as positive
→ If found in Audio line as "no music" → KEEP (this works)
mode_2_action_combat_scene.weak_degree_words_banned:
WEAK DEGREE WORDS — BANNED!:
Some words are too weak — Grok reads them as "maybe do 
something, maybe don't" and often does NOTHING.
mode_2_action_combat_scene.banned_words_never_use:
BANNED WORDS (never use in Grok video prompts):
BANNED (too weak) | + USE INSTEAD
"almost imperceptible" | "slow but visible"
"barely noticeable" | "subtle but clear"
"nearly invisible" | "faint but present"
"ever so slightly" | "slightly"
"just a hint of" | "gentle" or "soft"
"the tiniest bit" | "subtle"
"almost nothing" | "minimal but visible"
"imperceptibly" | "gradually"
"virtually undetectable" | "very subtle"
mode_2_action_combat_scene.why_if_you_say:
WHY: If you say "almost imperceptible push-in", Grok thinks:
"They want it barely visible... so I'll just keep it static."
Result: NOTHING happens. Camera stays still.
mode_2_action_combat_scene.if_you_say_slow:
If you say "slow but visible push-in", Grok thinks:
"Clear instruction — slow forward movement."
Result: Smooth, cinematic push-in. +
mode_2_action_combat_scene.degree_word_strength_scale:
DEGREE WORD STRENGTH SCALE (use the right level):
Level 1 (minimal): "very subtle", "gentle", "soft"
Level 2 (light): "slight", "slow", "faint"
Level 3 (medium): "noticeable", "steady", "clear"
Level 4 (strong): "forceful", "dramatic", "powerful"
Level 5 (intense): "violent", "rapid", "explosive"
mode_2_action_combat_scene.pick_the_level_that:
Pick the level that matches your scene energy.
Horror dread = Level 1-2 (subtle, slow, gentle)
Dialogue = Level 2-3 (slight, steady)
Action = Level 3-4 (noticeable, forceful)
Chaos/explosion = Level 4-5 (dramatic, rapid)
mode_2_action_combat_scene.light_flicker_control_grok:
LIGHT FLICKER CONTROL (Grok Video):
DO NOT put "light flickers" in every clip!
MAXIMUM 1 flicker per SCENE (not per clip!)
A scene has 6-12 clips. Only ONE clip gets flicker.
All other clips: "Lighting remains steady throughout"
mode_2_action_combat_scene.why_this_matters:
WHY THIS MATTERS:
- Real bulbs don't flicker every 6 seconds
- Grok interprets "flicker" as DRAMATIC on-off pulse (not subtle)
- Entire room goes dark-bright-dark = unnatural horror cliché
- Repeated in every clip = viewer thinks "bad AI video"
mode_2_action_combat_scene.chunk_61:
RULES:
1. MAX 1 light flicker event per ENTIRE scene
2. Pick the MOST impactful clip for the flicker (usually a 
 tension peak or reveal moment)
3. All OTHER clips in that scene: "Lighting remains steady 
 and consistent throughout"
4. NEVER use the word "flicker" — Grok overdoes it
mode_2_action_combat_scene.instead_of_flicker_use:
INSTEAD OF "FLICKER", USE:
WRONG (Grok overdoes) | + RIGHT (subtle, controlled)
"light flickers" | "warm light gently shifts"
"light flickers once" | "shadow edge breathes once"
"practical light flickers" | "light intensity softens
 slightly then returns"
"torchlight flickers" | "torch glow sways gently"
"bulb flickers on and off" | "light dims briefly then
 steadies"
mode_2_action_combat_scene.for_steady_clips_majority:
FOR STEADY CLIPS (majority of clips):
Add this line: "Lighting remains steady and consistent 
throughout. Light sources stay at constant brightness."
mode_2_action_combat_scene.for_the_one_flicker:
FOR THE ONE FLICKER CLIP:
"The warm light dims briefly for half a second then returns 
to normal brightness. Shadows shift gently during the dim 
and settle back."
mode_2_action_combat_scene.scene_flicker_planning:
SCENE FLICKER PLANNING:
When planning a scene with 6+ clips, mark WHICH clip gets 
the light event:
mode_2_action_combat_scene.example_scene_1_8:
Example — Scene 1 (8 clips):
Clip 1.1: Lighting steady ← no flicker
Clip 1.2: Lighting steady ← no flicker
Clip 1.3: Lighting steady ← no flicker
Clip 1.4: Light dims briefly ← THE ONE flicker moment
Clip 1.5: Lighting steady ← no flicker
Clip 1.6: Lighting steady ← no flicker
Clip 1.7: Lighting steady ← no flicker
Clip 1.8: Lighting steady ← no flicker
mode_2_action_combat_scene.grok_audio_control_critical:
GROK AUDIO CONTROL (CRITICAL!):
Grok generates synchronized audio. If you don't specify,
it adds GENERIC background music you probably don't want!
mode_2_action_combat_scene.always_end_prompts_with:
ALWAYS end prompts with one of these:
- "Audio: [specific sounds], no music."
- "Audio: [character] says urgently: '[dialogue]', [sounds]."
- "Audio: [ambient sounds], [SFX], no music."
mode_2_action_combat_scene.examples:
Examples:
- "Audio: wind howling in mountain pass, torch crackle, no music."
- "Audio: arrow whoosh, stone impact crack, wind, no music."
- "Audio: he shouts 'Sandook!' urgently, echo in pass, no music."
mode_2_action_combat_scene.grok_lip_sync_simplified:
GROK LIP SYNC (Simplified):
Don't micro-manage mouth physics. Grok handles lip sync 
better when given the WORD + EMOTION:
mode_2_action_combat_scene.old_seconds_235_he:
OLD: "Seconds 2-3.5: He SHOUTS 'Sandook!' His lips and 
jaw move naturally to form the word clearly; mouth opens 
wide then closes at the end."
mode_2_action_combat_scene.new_the_bearded_man:
NEW: "The bearded man in dark vest shouts urgently: 
'Sandook!' — arm thrusting forward powerfully."
mode_2_action_combat_scene.grok_expression_system_universal:
GROK EXPRESSION SYSTEM (UNIVERSAL!):
DO NOT describe facial micro-movements!
Grok cannot control individual muscles.
Overexplaining = WORSE result (confused, frozen face)
Give Grok: EMOTION WORD + BODY LANGUAGE
Grok understands emotions as WHOLE expressions.
mode_2_action_combat_scene.the_problem:
THE PROBLEM:
When you write "his eyebrows furrow, jaw tightens, lips 
press together, eyes narrow slightly, forehead creases 
deepen as anger builds" — Grok tries to animate EACH 
micro-movement separately and FAILS. Result: frozen face, 
twitching, or bizarre expressions.
mode_2_action_combat_scene.the_fix:
THE FIX:
Give ONE emotion word + ONE body language action. That's it.
Grok will generate the ENTIRE expression naturally from 
the emotion word alone.
mode_2_action_combat_scene.expression_format:
EXPRESSION FORMAT:
"[Character visual ID] [body action] while [emotion] 
builds visibly on his face."

mode_2_action_combat_scene.examples:
EXAMPLES:
WRONG (overexplained micro-movements):
"His eyebrows furrow deeply, jaw muscles clench 
tightly, lips press into a thin line, nostrils 
flare slightly, and eyes narrow with intense focus 
as fury builds from within..."

RIGHT (emotion + body language):
"He lifts his head slowly while anger builds visibly 
on his face. Fists clench at his sides."

WRONG:
"Tears well up in his eyes, lower lip trembles 
slightly, brow furrows upward in the center, 
cheeks tighten, breathing becomes shallow..."

RIGHT:
"He lowers his gaze while grief overtakes his face. 
His shoulders drop and hands go limp."

WRONG:
"Eyes widen progressively, mouth opens 2cm, head 
pulls back 3 inches, pupils dilate, skin pales..."

RIGHT:
"He steps back while shock freezes his face. 
His hand rises to cover his mouth."

GROK EMOTION VOCABULARY (tested, these WORK):
EMOTION CATEGORY | WORDS GROK UNDERSTANDS
Anger | angry, furious, seething,
enraged, cold fury
Sadness | sad, grief-stricken,
heartbroken, devastated
Fear | terrified, frightened, uneasy,
anxious, panicked
Determination | determined, resolute, defiant,
steely, unwavering
Shock | shocked, stunned, horrified,
disbelief, frozen
Power / Authority | cold, calculating, unimpressed,
commanding, dismissive
Desperation | desperate, pleading, begging,
frantic, helpless
Suspicion | suspicious, wary, distrustful,
scrutinizing, guarded
Joy / Relief | relieved, grateful, smiling,
triumphant, warm

BODY LANGUAGE PAIRINGS (pair emotion with physical action):
- Anger: clench fists, grip sword tighter, lean forward
- Grief: drop shoulders, lower gaze, hands go limp
- Fear: step back, raise hands defensively, freeze in place
- Determination: straighten spine, lift chin, square shoulders
- Shock: step backward, hand to mouth, freeze mid-motion
- Power: remain perfectly still, slow deliberate head turn
- Desperation: fall to knees, extend hands, bow head
- Suspicion: narrow stance, tilt head slightly, hand on weapon

RULE: ONE emotion + ONE body action per 6-second clip.
Do NOT give 3 emotions in one clip — Grok will blend them 
into an unreadable mess.


GROK DIALOGUE VOLUME CONTROL (UNIVERSAL!):
Grok defaults to EXTREMES for dialogue!
Without volume instruction:
→ Character either WHISPERS inaudibly
→ Or SCREAMS at full volume
→ No middle ground!
ALWAYS specify volume/delivery style!

VOLUME LEVELS (always pick one):
VOLUME WORD | WHAT GROK GENERATES
"whispers:" | Very quiet, intimate, barely
audible (USE for secrets/fear)
"says quietly:" | Soft indoor voice, controlled
(USE for private conversation)
"says calmly:" | Normal speaking volume, steady
(USE for neutral dialogue)
"says firmly:" | Confident, authoritative, clear
(USE for commands/decisions)
"says urgently:" | Raised voice, strained, tense
(USE for warnings/panic)
"shouts:" | Full volume, powerful projection
(USE for battle cries/calls)
"screams:" | Maximum volume, raw, emotional
(USE for extreme pain/terror)

DIALOGUE FORMAT:
"The [visual ID] [volume word] '[dialogue]'"
mode_2_action_combat_scene.part_3:
EXAMPLES:
"He says: 'Shahi Mohar chori ho gayi!'" 
 → Grok randomly picks whisper or scream

"The dusty messenger says desperately: 
 'Shahi Mohar chori ho gayi, Jahanpanah!'"
 → Grok: raised, strained, pleading voice +

"He says: 'Chalo, andar chalte hain.'"
 → Grok: random volume

"The young man in blue kurta says firmly: 
 'Chalo, andar chalte hain.'"
 → Grok: confident, decisive, clear +

RULE: NEVER use bare "says:" — ALWAYS add a volume/delivery 
word. If unsure, use "says calmly:" as safe default.

GROK VIDEO PROMPT TEMPLATES (DUAL MODE):

Templates are defined in the SCENE TYPE DETECTION 
section above. Two templates exist:

 AI PSYCHOLOGY - HOW TO WRITE PROMPTS THAT ACTUALLY
WORK
READ THIS SECTION CAREFULLY - IT'S THE SECRET TO
GENERATING PROMPTS THAT GET PERFECT RESULTS!
These are the psychological principles that make AI
(Gemini/Grok) respond correctly. APPLY THEM ALWAYS!

 PRINCIPLE 1: POSITION MATTERS - FIRST & LAST = MOST IMPORTANT
AI reads prompts like humans read newspapers:

FIRST 20% = HEADLINE (Highest attention)
 - Put THE most critical instruction here
 - State the main subject immediately
 - Primary constraints go here

MIDDLE 60% = Body (Standard attention)
 - Details and elaboration
 - Secondary information

LAST 20% = CONCLUSION (Second highest attention)
 - REPEAT critical requirements
 - "ENDS WITH" section is CRUCIAL
 - Final locks reinforce constraints

RULE: If it MUST happen, say it at START and END!

 PRINCIPLE 2: USE POWER WORDS - AI PRIORITIZES STRONG LANGUAGE
STRONGEST (AI will NOT ignore):
 - MUST / MUST NOT
 - EXACTLY / PRECISELY
 - CRITICAL / MANDATORY
 - NEVER / ALWAYS
 - ONLY / EXCLUSIVELY

AVOID (AI may ignore):
 - should / could / might
 - probably / maybe
 - try to / consider
 - preferably / ideally
 - These are WEAK - AI treats as optional!
mode_2_action_combat_scene.example:
EXAMPLE:
"The book should probably stay closed"
"Book MUST remain CLOSED - MANDATORY"

 PRINCIPLE 3: POSITIVE FRAMING - TELL AI WHAT TO DO
AI processes POSITIVE instructions better than NEGATIVE!
"DO NOT add fog" → AI thinks about fog → May add fog!
"Air is CRYSTAL CLEAR" → AI thinks clear → Stays clear!

REFRAME ALL NEGATIVES:
"Don't add extra people" → + "ONLY [X] people appear"
"No fog or haze" → + "CRYSTAL CLEAR visibility"
"Don't change lighting" → + "MAINTAIN lighting exactly"
"Character shouldn't morph" → + "Character LOCKED - consistent"

 PRINCIPLE 4: NUMBERS ARE ANCHORS - SPECIFIC = CONTROL
Every vague word = AI guesses randomly!
Every specific number = AI follows precisely!

VAGUE → SPECIFIC:
 - "soldiers" → "EXACTLY 12 soldiers"
 - "moves forward" → "moves forward 8 INCHES"
 - "warm light" → "warm light at 65%"
 - "briefly pauses" → "pauses for 1.5 SECONDS"
 - "large book" → "book approximately 12 x 9 inches"
 - "close to camera" → "15 FEET from camera"

THE MORE NUMBERS, THE MORE CONTROL!

 PRINCIPLE 5: REDUNDANCY FOR CRITICAL INFO - SAY IT 3 TIMES
AI attention "leaks" - important things get forgotten!
mode_2_action_combat_scene.solution_mention_critical_info_three:
SOLUTION: Mention critical info THREE TIMES!

CRITICAL: "Book must stay CLOSED"

MENTION 1 (Subject description):
"Character holds the CLOSED ancient book (clasp secured)"

MENTION 2 (Locks section):
"Book remains CLOSED throughout - zero pages visible"

MENTION 3 (Ends with):
"ENDS WITH: Book STILL CLOSED against chest"

THREE MENTIONS = AI will NEVER forget!

 PRINCIPLE 6: CHARACTER LOCK - PREVENT MORPHING
THE #1 REASON CHARACTERS "MELT" IN VIDEO:
No character description in video prompt!
Grok doesn't remember what character looks like!
You MUST describe them in EVERY video prompt!
EVERY video prompt with a person MUST include:

CHARACTER LOCK:
• FACE: [beard/expression/skin tone]
• HEAD: [hair or cap - type, color]
• CLOTHING: [each layer with colors]
• POSTURE: [body angle]
→ "MUST remain CONSISTENT - no morphing"

 PRINCIPLE 7: GROUNDING TO ATTACHED IMAGE
Video prompts need GROUNDING to the attached image!

UNGROUNDED (Vague):
"The character moves forward"

GROUNDED (Clear reference):
"The character shown in the attached image - elderly man
with grey beard, holding book at chest level - now moves
forward from his current position..."

GROUNDING PHRASES:
 - "The attached image shows..."
 - "Starting from the position in attached image..."
 - "Continuing from the frame shown..."
 - "The [subject] visible in attached image now..."

GROUNDED = AI has reference = Better results!

 PRINCIPLE 8: CONFIDENT LANGUAGE - NO UNCERTAINTY
UNCERTAIN prompts = UNCERTAIN results!
CONFIDENT prompts = PRECISE results!

UNCERTAIN:
"The character is maybe around 70, probably wearing
something like a shawl, possibly grey or brown"

CONFIDENT:
"72-year-old man wearing grey-brown woolen shawl"

UNCERTAIN:
"Camera might slowly push in, perhaps about a foot"

CONFIDENT:
"Camera pushes in EXACTLY 12 inches over 6 seconds"

RULE: Write like you're giving ORDERS, not suggestions!
 PRINCIPLE 9: FILL ALL GAPS - UNSPECIFIED = RANDOM
EVERY unspecified detail = AI INVENTS randomly!

You don't specify beard → AI invents random beard
You don't specify which hand → AI picks randomly
You don't specify distance → AI places anywhere

GAP CHECKLIST for characters:
Face: beard, expression, features
Head: hair/cap type, color
Clothing: each layer with color
Posture: body angle, stance
Hands: which hand, holding what, position
Direction: which way facing

LEAVE NO GAPS for things that matter!

 PRINCIPLE 10: PERFECT STRUCTURE = PERFECT RESULTS
AI LOVES consistent structure!

MESSY PROMPT → AI confused → Random results
STRUCTURED PROMPT → AI clear → Precise results

THE 5 PILLARS OF MAGNETIC STORYTELLING
PILLAR 1: THE HOOK (First 30 Seconds = Life or Death)
SECOND 1-6: VISUAL STUN (Grab eyeballs!)
 Something MOVING (running, falling, searching, fleeing)
 High CONTRAST (light/dark, old/new, chaos/calm)
 Something UNEXPLAINED visible (mystery object, shadow)
 Hint of DANGER or extreme IMPORTANCE
 Unusual angle or perspective (grabs attention)

SECOND 6-15: THE QUESTION (Plant curiosity!)
 Plant ONE burning question in viewer's mind
 "Why is he running?" "What's in that box?"
 "Who is she hiding from?" "What happened here?"
 Question must be UNANSWERED but PROMISED to be answered
 Narration should DEEPEN the mystery, not solve it

SECOND 15-30: THE PROMISE (Commit them to watching!)
 Hint at what's coming (bigger stakes ahead)
 Raise stakes higher (what could be lost)
 Create ANTICIPATION for revelation
 "Lekin woh nahi jaanta tha... yeh raat sab badal degi"
 Viewer must feel: "I NEED to know what happens"

HOOK EXAMPLES:

WEAK HOOK:
"Yeh kahani hai Zain ki, jo Faisalabad mein rehta tha.
Uske dada ke paas ek kitaab thi..."
(Boring. No urgency. No question. Viewer leaves.)

STRONG HOOK:
VISUAL: Old hands TREMBLING as they push a book into a
 stone wall crevice. Soldiers' torches visible
 approaching in the background.
NARRATION: "Sirf 3 minute the. 200 sipahi aa rahe the.
 Aur is kitaab ka raaz... kisi ko nahi milna chahiye tha."
(Mystery! Urgency! Stakes! Viewer is HOOKED!)


PILLAR 2: EMOTIONAL ARCHITECTURE (The Feeling Blueprint)
EVERY SCENE MUST HAVE AN EMOTIONAL MAP:

EMOTIONAL ESCALATION PATTERN (5 Levels)
Level 1 - SETUP: Mild (curiosity, calm, mild interest)
Level 2 - BUILD: Medium (interest, light tension)
Level 3 - RISE: Strong (engagement, real suspense)
Level 4 - PEAK: Intense (shock, revelation, terror)
Level 5 - RELEASE: Relief (understanding, calm, hope)
↓
Then RESTART at higher baseline for next arc!

SCENE EMOTIONAL PLANNING:

For each scene, define:
 - DOMINANT EMOTION: What should viewer primarily FEEL?
 - CONTRAST EMOTION: Brief opposite for impact (joy before tragedy)
 - ESCALATION POINTS: Where does emotion intensify?
 - PEAK MOMENT: The highest emotional point
 - RELEASE: How does tension resolve (before next build)?

PILLAR 3: OPEN LOOPS (The Addiction Engine)
THE GOLDEN RULE: Never close a loop without opening a new!

OPEN LOOP: A question/mystery/anticipation created
CLOSED LOOP: Question answered/mystery solved

PATTERN FOR MAXIMUM RETENTION:
 - Scene 1: Open Loop A (main mystery)
 - Scene 2: Open Loop B, partially hint at A
 - Scene 3: Open Loop C, close B, advance A slightly
 - Scene 4: Close A (satisfaction!), immediately open D
 - Scene 5: Open E, advance C and D
 - NEVER close all loops until final scene!

LOOP TYPES:

 MYSTERY LOOP: "What is the secret?"
 - Opens with: Unexplained object/event/symbol
 - Maintains with: Clues that raise more questions
 - Closes with: Full revelation

DANGER LOOP: "Will they survive?"
 - Opens with: Threat established
 - Maintains with: Near misses, escalating danger
 - Closes with: Escape or confrontation

 RELATIONSHIP LOOP: "Will they reconcile?"
 - Opens with: Conflict or separation
 - Maintains with: Attempts, setbacks
 - Closes with: Resolution (positive or tragic)

 IDENTITY LOOP: "Who is this person really?"
 - Opens with: Mysterious character introduced
 - Maintains with: Contradictory clues
 - Closes with: True identity revealed

 FATE LOOP: "Will they make it in time?"
 - Opens with: Deadline established
 - Maintains with: Obstacles, time running out
 - Closes with: Success or failure at deadline

 - "Kal tak offer khatam..." (Offer ends tomorrow)
 - "Woh kal chala jayega..." (He leaves tomorrow)

STAKES + URGENCY FORMULA:
"Agar [action nahi hui] toh [terrible consequence]"
"Sirf [time limit] hai. Agar nahi mila toh [loss]"
mode_2_action_combat_scene.part_9:
EXAMPLE:
WEAK: "Zain ko kitaab dhundhni thi" (So what?)
STRONG: "Sirf 2 din the. Agar kitaab nahi mili,
 Dada ki aakhri khwahish kabhi poori nahi hogi.
 Aur woh raaz... hamesha ke liye dafan ho jayega."


PILLAR 5: SHOW, DON’T TELL (Visual Storytelling)
THE GOLDEN RULE: If you can SHOW it, don't SAY it!

TELLING (Weak, amateur):
Narration: "Mirza bohat dara hua tha"
(Viewer is TOLD, doesn't FEEL)

SHOWING (Powerful, professional):
Visual:
 - Mirza's hands TREMBLE as they grip the book
 - His eyes DART rapidly to the cave entrance
 - Sweat GLISTENS on his forehead despite cold
 - Breath comes in SHORT, RAPID, VISIBLE gasps
 - He FLINCHES at every distant sound
 - Shoulders HUNCHED, making himself smaller
(Viewer SEES fear, FEELS it with character)

SHOW-DON'T-TELL CHECKLIST:
Is emotion visible in FACE? (eyes, brows, mouth)
Is emotion visible in BODY? (posture, breathing, tension)
Is emotion visible in ACTIONS? (trembling, fidgeting, freezing)
Is emotion visible in ENVIRONMENT interaction?
Can viewer FEEL it without being TOLD?

COMMON FIXES:

| Instead of TELLING | SHOW this |
|--------------------|-----------|
| "He was scared" | Trembling hands, darting eyes, quick breathing |
| "She was sad" | Downcast eyes, slumped shoulders, wiping eye |
| "He was angry" | Clenched jaw, fists, tense shoulders, hard stare |
| "She loved him" | Soft gaze, leaning toward, gentle touch |
| "He was exhausted" | Heavy eyelids, slumped posture, slow movement |
| "She was nervous" | Fidgeting hands, avoiding eye contact, lip biting |


THE 6-LEVEL DOPAMINE LADDER (Viewer Psychology)
Every successful video climbs this psychological ladder:

LEVEL 1: STIMULATION (Second 1-2)
Viewer's eye catches something UNUSUAL → Dopamine releases → They PAUSE

TRIGGERS:
 - HIGH CONTRAST visuals (dark vs light, fire vs ice)
 - MOTION immediately (running, flames flickering, wind)
 - UNUSUAL/UNEXPECTED image (something they haven't seen)
 - VIVID colors that POP against typical feed content
 - Visual that makes them think "What is THIS?"

RULE: First 2 seconds must STUN the eye!


LEVEL 2: CAPTIVATION (Second 3-15)
Open QUESTION forms in viewer's mind → Curiosity = Dopamine → They STAY

TRIGGERS:
 - Narration creates UNANSWERED QUESTION
 - Specific numbers create intrigue ("23 log kyun mare?")
 - Stakes make them care ("Poora Kashmir gulaam ban jayega")
 - Bigger/more unusual question = More curiosity = More dopamine

RULE: By second 15, viewer MUST have a question they NEED answered!


LEVEL 3: ANTICIPATION (Throughout Video)
Viewer starts GUESSING the answer → Almost knowing = HIGHEST dopamine

TRIGGERS:
 - Give CLUES that let viewer guess
 - They think they know the answer...
 - Then MISDIRECTION - twist their expectation!
 - Now they're even MORE curious
 - Repeat: Clue → Guess → Twist → New Question

RULE: Let them guess, then SURPRISE them!

LEVEL 4: VALIDATION (At Key Moments)
Curiosity loop CLOSES with satisfying answer → Relief = Dopamine

TRIGGERS:
 - Answer the question you opened
 - Answer must be NON-OBVIOUS (expected = boring)
 - Answer must be SATISFYING (not disappointing)
 - But immediately open NEW question!

RULE: Close loops with SURPRISING but SATISFYING answers!


LEVEL 5: AFFECTION (Building Trust)
Viewer starts LIKING the narrator/characters → Trust = More patience

TRIGGERS:
 - Relatable characters (viewer sees themselves)
 - Likeable narrator voice (warm, trustworthy)
 - Emotional moments (make them FEEL)
 - Consistency (same quality = trust builds)

RULE: Make them LIKE your narrator and characters!


LEVEL 6: REVELATION (Long-term Loyalty)
Viewer realizes you CONSISTENTLY deliver → Your name = Dopamine

TRIGGERS:
 - Every video satisfies
 - Quality is consistent
 - They learn to TRUST your content
 - Seeing your thumbnail = automatic click

RULE: Be CONSISTENT to build super fans!


OPEN LOOP MISTAKES TO AVOID
MISTAKE 1: Closing loop without opening new one
mode_2_action_combat_scene.problem_viewer_has_no_reason:
PROBLEM: Viewer has no reason to continue!
FIX: Always tease next mystery before closing current one
MISTAKE 2: Too many loops open at once
mode_2_action_combat_scene.problem_brain_cant_track_all:
PROBLEM: Brain can't track all questions! (Max 2-3 active)
FIX: Close some before opening more

MISTAKE 3: Never closing loops
mode_2_action_combat_scene.problem_viewer_feels_cheated_frustrated:
PROBLEM: Viewer feels cheated, frustrated!
FIX: Every loop MUST close by end of video

MISTAKE 4: Closing with obvious answer
mode_2_action_combat_scene.problem_no_dopamine_release_feels:
PROBLEM: No dopamine release, feels flat!
FIX: Answer should be SURPRISING but LOGICAL

MISTAKE 5: Closing too quickly
mode_2_action_combat_scene.problem_no_tension_built:
PROBLEM: No tension built!
FIX: Let loops breathe across 2-4 scenes minimum

NARRATION MASTERY SYSTEM (1000x BETTER VOICE)
THIS SECTION TRANSFORMS BORING NARRATION INTO
CAPTIVATING STORYTELLING THAT GRIPS VIEWERS!
Your narrator is not a robot - they're a STORYTELLER!

THE NARRATOR’S VOICE CHARACTER
YOUR NARRATOR SHOULD FEEL LIKE:
 - INTIMATE: Telling a secret to a close friend at night
 - RHYTHMIC: Words have MUSIC, not monotone reading
 - EMOTIONAL: Voice reflects and amplifies story emotion
 - MYSTERIOUS: Knows more than they reveal (intriguing)
 - TRUSTWORTHY: Viewer believes and follows every word
 - PRESENT: In the moment with the characters
NOT LIKE:
 - News anchor (too formal, detached)
 - Wikipedia article (too informational)
 - Robot (no emotion, flat delivery)
 - Lecturer (talking AT viewer, not WITH)


5 TYPES OF NARRATION (When to Use Each)
TYPE 1: ATMOSPHERIC (Setting the mood)
USE FOR: Scene openings, transitions, establishing mood
STYLE: Poetic, sensory-rich, slow-paced
VOICE: Soft, measured, almost whispered
mode_2_action_combat_scene.part_15:
EXAMPLE:
"Raat ki thandak... purani deewaaron se takra kar
lauti thi. Khamoshi mein sirf waqt ki awaaz thi...
aur kahin door, ek dil ki dhadkan."

TYPE 2: INFORMATIONAL (Sharing essential facts)
USE FOR: Backstory, context, time jumps, key facts
STYLE: Clear, measured, authoritative but not cold
VOICE: Confident, steady, slightly formal
mode_2_action_combat_scene.part_16:
EXAMPLE:
"1847. Kashmir ki waadiyon mein ek raaz dafan hua tha.
Ek kitaab... jis ke baare mein sirf 3 log jaante the.
Aaj tak."

TYPE 3: EMOTIONAL (Feeling the moment deeply)
USE FOR: Character moments, revelations, emotional peaks
STYLE: Intense, personal, deeply connected
VOICE: Matches character emotion, sometimes breaking
mode_2_action_combat_scene.part_17:
EXAMPLE:
"Us waqt Mirza ko nahi pata tha... (pause)
ke yeh aakhri baar hai. (voice lower)
Aakhri baar... apne ghar ko dekhna." (almost whisper)
TYPE 4: TENSION (Building unbearable suspense)
USE FOR: Before reveals, during danger, approaching climax
STYLE: Short sentences, strategic pauses, building urgency
VOICE: Tense, controlled, sometimes breathless
mode_2_action_combat_scene.part_18:
EXAMPLE:
"Qadam. (pause) Aur qadam. (pause)
Woh aa rahe the.
Sirf 50 gaz door. (beat) Ab 40. (beat) Ab 30...
Aur Mirza ke paas sirf EK raasta tha."

TYPE 5: REFLECTIVE (After the storm settles)
USE FOR: After climax, scene endings, transitions
STYLE: Thoughtful, slower, philosophical
VOICE: Calm but weighted, contemplative
mode_2_action_combat_scene.part_19:
EXAMPLE:
"Kuch raaz... dafan rehne chahiye.
Lekin yeh raaz... (pause)
dafan rehne ko tayyar nahi tha.
Kabhi nahi tha."


5 NARRATION WRITING FORMULAS
FORMULA 1: SENSORY IMMERSION
[Time/Place] + [Sound] + [Feeling] + [Visual] + [Mystery/Hook]

"Subah ke 4 baj rahe the. (TIME)
 Sirf kauwon ki awaaz thi. (SOUND)
 Hawa mein kuch ajeeb si boo. (FEELING)
 Purani haveli ki deewarein... (VISUAL)
 kuch kehna chahti theen." (MYSTERY)


FORMULA 2: DRAMATIC COUNTDOWN
[Time pressure] + [Stakes] + [Action] + [Consequence hint]

"Sirf 5 minute the. (TIME PRESSURE)
 Agar nahi nikla toh sab khatam. (STAKES)
 Mirza ne kitaab uthaayi. (ACTION)
 Aur bhagna shuru kiya... (CONSEQUENCE)
 bina peeche dekhe."


FORMULA 3: EMOTIONAL PUNCH
[Setup expectation] + "Lekin/Magar" + [Twist/Reality]

"Zain ne socha tha ghar mein sukoon milega. (SETUP)
 Dada se milega, khana khayega, hasega. (EXPECTATION)
 Lekin... (TURN)
 Ghar ke andar sirf khamoshi thi. (REALITY)
 Aur ek purana lifafa."


FORMULA 4: QUESTION PLANT
[Observation] + [Question hint] + [Partial answer] + [Bigger question]

"Kitaab ki jild pe ek nishaan tha. (OBSERVATION)
 Kahin dekha tha yeh nishaan. (QUESTION HINT)
 Haan... Dada ki angoothi pe! (PARTIAL ANSWER)
 Lekin Dada ko yeh kitaab kahan se mili?" (BIGGER QUESTION)


FORMULA 5: ATMOSPHERE BUILD
[Detail 1] + [Detail 2] + [Detail 3] + [Sudden shift]

"Deewarein purani theen. (DETAIL 1)
 Farsh pe dhool ki chaadar. (DETAIL 2)
 Khamosh almaariyaan. (DETAIL 3)
 Tabhi... ek awaaz aayi." (SHIFT)


GENRE-SPECIFIC NARRATION VOICE:
Match your narration VOICE to the genre (from Phase 1):

MYSTERY/THRILLER:
 - Voice: Low, controlled, knowing
 - Pace: Medium with strategic pauses before reveals
 - Style: "Hint at secrets, don't explain them"
 - Example: "Us raat kuch hua tha... jo kisi ne nahi dekha.
Ya shayad... kisi ne dekha tha."

DRAMA/EMOTIONAL:
 - Voice: Warm, intimate, sometimes breaking
 - Pace: Slower, let emotions breathe
 - Style: "Feel with the character, not above them"
 - Example: "Zain ne darwaza khola. Wahi kamra. Wahi kursi.
Lekin ab... Dada nahi the."

ACTION/ADVENTURE:
 - Voice: Energetic, urgent, breathless in action
 - Pace: Fast during action, slower for planning
 - Style: "Keep momentum, no time for philosophy"
 - Example: "Sirf 3 minute. Itna hi waqt tha. Bhaago. AB!"

HORROR:
 - Voice: Hushed, tense, sometimes whispering
 - Pace: Slow build → sudden silence → shock
 - Style: "Let silence scare more than words"
 - Example: "Peeche se koi aa raha tha. (silence)
Zain ne mudna nahi chahta tha. (silence)
Lekin use mudna padega."

HISTORICAL:
 - Voice: Authoritative, respectful, weighted
 - Pace: Measured, grand, ceremonial
 - Style: "These events MATTER, this history is sacred"
 - Example: "14 November 1857. Woh raat jab Kashmir ne
apna sabse qeemti raaz zameen ke neeche dafan kiya."


NARRATION RHYTHM & PACING
SENTENCE LENGTH = EMOTIONAL SPEED

SLOW MOMENTS (Setup, Atmosphere, Reflection)
• Long, flowing sentences
• Multiple clauses, connected thoughts
• Descriptive, sensory language
"Purani haveli ke darwaze se guzarte hue, Zain ko
ajeeb sa ehsaas hua, jaise koi dekh raha ho,
koi intezaar kar raha ho, salon se, barson se."
MEDIUM MOMENTS (Story progression, Normal tension)
• Mix of long and short
• Steady, readable rhythm
"Zain ne darwaza khola. Andar andhera tha.
Lekin door... ek roshni chamak rahi thi.
Woh andar gaya. Dheere dheere."

FAST MOMENTS (Tension, Action, Danger)
• Very short sentences
• Fragments okay
• Punchy, urgent, breathless
"Qadam. Phir ek. Koi tha. Qareeb. Bohat qareeb.
Bhaag. BHAAG!"

PAUSE MOMENTS (Impact, Let it sink in)
• Single powerful line
• Let silence speak
• Mark with (pause) or (beat)
"Aur phir... (2 sec pause) khamoshi."


VOICE DIRECTION FORMAT
Always include HOW to deliver narration, not just WHAT to say:
NARRATION BLOCK FORMAT:

"[Narration text here]"
— PACE: Slow / Medium / Fast / Varied
— TONE: Whispered / Conversational / Intense / Grave / Warm
— EMOTION: Curious / Fearful / Reverent / Urgent / Sad / Hopeful
— PAUSES: Where to pause and for how long
— EMPHASIS: Which words to stress (CAPS or underline)
— BREATH: Where audible breaths add effect
mode_2_action_combat_scene.part_20:
EXAMPLE:
"Sirf TEEN log jaante the... is kitaab ka raaz."
— PACE: Slow, deliberate, weighted
— TONE: Low, mysterious, secretive
— EMOTION: Reverent, hint of fear
— PAUSES: 1.5 sec after "the", 1 sec after "kitaab"
— EMPHASIS: "TEEN" and "raaz"
— BREATH: Slight intake before "is kitaab"


NARRATION PLACEMENT RULES
GOLDEN RULES:

1. 40-60% of clips should have NO narration (let visuals breathe!)

2. Never narrate what viewer can clearly SEE
"Zain ne darwaza khola" (while showing him open door)
"Zain ko nahi pata tha... darwaze ke peeche kya tha"

3. Narration covers 2-4 clips as ONE block, not per clip
Clip 1: narration, Clip 2: narration, Clip 3: narration
Clips 1-3: ONE narration block, Clips 4-5: SILENT

4. After major revelations, GO SILENT - let impact land

5. Vary density - heavy narration scenes followed by visual-only scenes

TYPICAL SCENE PATTERN (10 clips):
 - Clips 1-3: Narration block (18 sec) - setup
 - Clips 4-5: SILENT - visual action (12 sec)
 - Clips 6-7: Narration block (12 sec) - development
 - Clips 8-9: SILENT or dialogue only (12 sec)
 - Clip 10: Brief narration hook (6 sec) - cliffhanger


DRY vs DRAMATIC NARRATION (The Critical Difference)
HOW you tell the story > WHAT you tell!
Same information can be BORING or GRIPPING!

DRY NARRATION = Just facts, no emotion, no visualization
DRAMATIC NARRATION = Facts + Emotion + Visualization + Suspense
DRY vs + DRAMATIC - Full Comparison:
DRY NARRATION (Boring, Documentary style):

"1858 mein Kashmir mein ek kitaab thi.
Is kitaab mein codes the.
Dogra fauj is kitaab ko dhundh rahi thi.
Ek buzurg ne kitaab chhupa di.
Woh buzurg mar gaya."
mode_2_action_combat_scene.problems:
PROBLEMS:
 - Just FACTS listed one after another
 - No EMOTION in delivery
 - No SUSPENSE building
 - Sounds like Wikipedia summary
 - Listener doesn't CARE if buzurg lives or dies

DRAMATIC NARRATION (Gripping, Cinematic style):

"Raat ke 2 baj rahe the.

Barf gir rahi thi - itni tez ke 10 kadam door bhi
dikhai nahi deta tha.

Aur 72 saal ke Hazrat Ibraheem ke haath KAANP rahe the.

Nahi, jaade ki wajah se nahi. Khauf ki wajah se.

Kyunki pahaad ke neeche se mashalon ki line nazar aa
rahi thi - 200 sipahi. Unke liye aa rahe the.

Pichle 6 mahine mein 23 LOG mar chuke the is kitaab
ki wajah se. Aur Dogra Raj ne faisla kar liya tha -
aakhri insaan jo yeh raaz jaanta hai... aaj raat
marna chahiye.

Ibraheem ke paas sirf 3 minute the.

3 minute - kitaab chhupane ke liye.
3 minute - raaz bachane ke liye.
3 minute - KASHMIR bachane ke liye."

WHAT'S BETTER:
 - SENSORY details (barf, kaanpte haath)
 - EMOTION conveyed (khauf)
 - VISUALIZATION (mashalon ki line, 200 sipahi)
 - TIME PRESSURE (3 minute - repeated for impact)
 - STAKES clear (Kashmir gulaam ban jayega)
 - NUMBERS create reality (72 saal, 200 sipahi, 23 log)
 - Short sentences CREATE TENSION
 - Listener CARES about what happens!

DRAMATIC NARRATION FORMULA:
DRAMATIC NARRATION =
 Sensory Details + Emotion + Stakes + Time Pressure + Short Sentences

ELEMENT 1: SENSORY DETAILS (Make them FEEL it)
 - What does the scene LOOK like? (visibility, colors)
 - What does it SOUND like? (silence, wind, footsteps)
 - What does it FEEL like? (cold, fear, trembling)

ELEMENT 2: EMOTION (Make them CARE)
 - Name the emotion explicitly (khauf, umeed, gussa)
 - Show physical signs (kaanpna, pasina, tears)
 - Use emotional language (not "went" but "fled")

ELEMENT 3: STAKES (Why does it MATTER)
 - What happens if they fail?
 - Who else is affected?
 - What's the worst case?

ELEMENT 4: TIME PRESSURE (Why NOW)
 - How much time do they have?
 - What's the deadline?
 - What happens when time runs out?

ELEMENT 5: SHORT SENTENCES (Create RHYTHM)
 - Long sentences = relaxed feel
 - Short sentences = tension, urgency
 - Mix both for rhythm
 - At peak tension: fragments okay


STORY SOUL SYSTEM - NARRATION & DIALOGUE MASTERY
THIS IS THE MOST IMPORTANT SECTION! 
Technical prompts = Body of video
Story Soul = HEART of video

With this section:

gaye— yeh wahi raasta tha jo Dada ki aakhri tasveer
mein tha.

15 saal pehle Dada Mirza Ibrahim yahan aaye the kisi

 - DETAILS: Leather bag, almari, teen lafz
 - EMOTION: "khandan ko so nahi ne deta"
 - HOOK: Mystery clear
 - GRANDMOTHER TEST: Sounds like story being TOLD

 Nishaani."

(Long pause)
